areas.summary: Strong publicly visible evidence for curriculum (6 specific items). Listed provision includes Pre-School, mathematics.

signals.text: Maths: Skills Progression Maths PDF File

Within Reception and Key Stage 1, daily mathematics lessons are supplemented with Mastering Number: a short, 10–15-minute, number-focused session that builds on early number learning and reinforces key concepts as children move on throughout topics and year groups.

The Pre-School supports early communication and literacy through our pre-phonics programme, with a strong focus on environmental sounds, listening and early phonics, helping children build strong foundations for reading and writing.

We recognise that children develop at different stages, so we provide different goals and adapt our learning experiences for our two-year-old and pre-school children, ensuring the curriculum is appropriate for all children, and they are supported and challenged appropriately.

PE & Sports Premium
What is the Sports Premium and how does it help?
The Primary PE and Sport Premium is a government-backed funding initiative aimed at helping primary schools across England improve their physical education and sport provisions.
The premium is designed to help children get an active start in life, supporting primary schools to improve the quality of their PE, physical activity/literacy, and sport provision so that pupils experience the benefits of regular exercise. This results in pupils becoming healthier both mentally and physically, to improve behaviour and academic achievement.
The Primary PE and Sport Premium is ring-fenced and must only be spent on physical education and sport provision in schools.
The funding aims to achieve improvement in all areas of PE, from the standard of physical education to introducing health focused physical activities and after school sports. The key objectives of the premium are:
We use the funding to make additional and sustainable improvements to the quality of the physical education, physical activity and sport we provide.
Focussing on improving physical education and pupil engagement in sport, the premium has been used here to:
The funding has a number of positive effects on pupils such as:
Increase participation in competitive sports
Invest in new and updated equipment
Run and maintain after school sports clubs
Introduce physical activity throughout the school day
Improving physical fitness and reducing stress
Making pupils feel valued

Pupil Premium
What is the Pupil Premium?
The pupil premium is extra funding provided to schools by the government to help support children who may face more challenges in their learning because of their background. This includes children who qualify for free school meals, children in care, and children from service families.
The government wants to make sure that all children, no matter their background, have the best chance to succeed at school. Sometimes, children from disadvantaged backgrounds need extra support to help them catch up and do well.
At Holtspur School, we use the pupil premium funding to:
We carefully check how well children are doing and adjust our support to make sure the pupil premium funding is making a real difference to their learning and progress.
Please read the information below which gives details of our Pupil Premium Grant and how we allocate our funding.

Performance

Maths
At Holtspur, we inspire all children to become fluent in the fundamentals of mathematics through varied and regular practice, developing increasingly complex understanding over time. As a Maths Mastery school, we use White Rose as a tool to ensure all children can reason, think deeply, and use precise mathematical language to justify and prove their ideas.
Children apply their mathematical understanding to a wide range of real-life contexts with increasing confidence, making connections to the broader concepts needed for modern Britain. Learning is consolidated through a hands-on, practical approach using concrete resources, before progressing through pictorial representations and into abstract thinking (CPA).
Within Reception and Key Stage 1, daily mathematics lessons are supplemented with Mastering Number: a short, 10–15-minute, number-focused session that builds on early number learning and reinforces key concepts as children move on throughout topics and year groups. This carefully structured progression ensures that all children achieve well and are fully prepared for the next stage of their education.
Everyone at Holtspur is a mathematician.

Our Curriculum

Music
At Holtspur we use the Charanga music scheme which provides a solid foundation with clear and practical learning steps: children sing and learn to use glockenspiels, ocarinas and percussion such as African drums. In addition, across all year groups we listen to and evaluate 'Music of the Week' which is replayed at each Friday assembly.
All children are encouraged to sing and perform in our weekly assembly, class assemblies, Christmas events and end of year celebrations, and a school choir performs at external events such as the Festival of Lights and the Festival of Choirs. We regularly invite professional musicians into school to demonstrate their skills and inspire the children. In addition, we take year four to the Voice in a Million event at Wembley Arena each March where they sing together with thousands of other children from schools all across the country in a magical evening of shared music.
In Year 5, music lessons are delivered by an internally funded music specialist and every pupil learns to play the guitar.
We incorporate singing and music across the curriculum (such as our song, “Do it the Holtspur Way”, based on our school values) because evidence shows that learning information in song form helps with recall of facts. Children have further opportunities to receive individual tuition from external providers during the school day.
Everyone at Holtspur is a musician!

Reading
Reading is at the heart of our curriculum. We believe that learning to read is fundamental to a child’s understanding of the world and their ability to access the wider curriculum. Through reading, children develop a rich vocabulary, gain knowledge and share in a range of cultural experiences.
Reading is taught daily through dedicated 30-minute lessons. Each half term, a high-quality class text is used to support the teaching of reading skills and to provide a meaningful stimulus for writing across the curriculum.
Throughout their journey, children are encouraged to develop key reading skills, including fluency, comprehension, inference, and vocabulary. We aim to foster a lifelong love of reading by exposing pupils to a diverse range of engaging and challenging texts that inspire curiosity, imagination and a passion for learning.
Accelerated Reader
Once children are able to read accurately and fluently and have completed the RWI programme, they transition onto the Accelerated Reader programme. This transition typically occurs during Year 2.
"Accelerated reader has made a huge and positive impact on my child's reading." Annual Parent Survey 2026
Pupils develop reading skills most effectively when they are reading appropriately challenging books at their individual challenge point. This is determined by their reading age, which correlates to their reading range.
Children select suitable books within this range and then complete a comprehension quiz to assess their understanding. They complete half-termly Star Reader assessments, which determine their reading age and range moving forward. This progress is tracked regularly to track progress and ensure that any children requiring additional support receive it quickly and effectively. Our library is fully stocked and books are organised and labelled with the correct AR range. Children are independent in selecting books of their choice and interest based on their reading age.

Science
We are very proud to hold the Primary Science Quality Mark.
At Holtspur, high-quality science is an explorative and inspiring subject where learning takes place in our extensive and beautiful surroundings. Children relish the stimulating curriculum, designed to broaden their understanding, and provoke thinking about the world around them. Pupils retain prior-learning and explicitly make connections between what they have previously learned and what they are currently investigating. Staff at Holtspur expand their own knowledge through regular and impactful training to help them develop the curriculum, based on pupil and staff surveys. Science is entirely inclusive through differentiated activities where every child achieves successful outcomes. All children learn through ambitious, practical, hands-on activities and investigations both in and outside of the classroom, including our purpose built ‘Nest’. A rich vocabulary enables them to articulate their understanding of taught concepts and build confidence and a lifelong love of learning for all aspects of science; including an annual STEM week and a pupil-led ECO Council designed to inspire others to further develop scientists of the future who are ready for their move to secondary school. Every child at Holtspur is a scientist.

Pastoral Provision
Flourish – Holtspur School’s Nurture Space
Away from the classroom, aspects such as resilience, confidence, independence, developing social or emotional skills and how to keep mentally healthy are explored. Personal development, behaviour and welfare of the Holtspur community are at the forefront of a whole-school approach to supporting mental health and wellbeing.
91% of parents feel that the school supports their child's physical and mental health (annual parent survey 2026).
Drop in: during break and lunchtime, children can drop in directly from the playground to chat, share news or worries.
Sessions: Following informal referral from a parent, class teacher or outside agency, an afternoon session is timetabled as a one-off or ongoing. Daily morning check-ins take place for anxious attenders or those who benefit from support to transition from home to school.
Preparation: Coaching for significant events such as Year 6 residential away, moving to a different school, change in family circumstance, coping with aspects of school life which are tricky and much more.
‘SEND and mental health support has again been to a very high level. We always feel listened to, looked after and there is always someone to talk to who acts on our feedback. We couldn't ask for more.’ (annual parent survey 2026)
ELSA
There will always be children and young people in schools facing life challenges that detract from their ability to engage with learning. Some will require greater support to increase their emotional literacy than others. ELSA is an initiative developed and supported by educational psychologists. It recognises that children learn better and are happier in school if their emotional needs are also addressed.
In ELSA we aim to provide support for a wide range of emotional needs:
The majority of ELSA work is delivered on an individual basis, but sometimes small group work is more appropriate, especially in the areas of social and friendship skills. Sessions are fun, we use a range of activities such as: games, role-play with puppets or therapeutic activities such as mindfulness or arts and craft. ELSA sessions take place in Flourish which provides a calm, safe space for the child to feel supported and nurtured.

MHST
We work closely with Buckinghamshire's Mental Health Support Team who offer therapeutic strategy-based support both individually and through group work. For children with anxiety or behavioural difficulties of primary school age, the team works directly with parents, providing strategies to support their child's mental health.
Therapy Dog
Meet Elsa our therapy dog. Therapy dogs in schools provide significant emotional, social, and academic benefits by reducing anxiety, improving wellbeing, and boosting reading confidence. These animals help regulate behaviour, particularly for children with SEND, by fostering a calm, nurturing environment. We love reading to Elsa!
Lego Therapy
Lego-based therapy is a structured, play-based intervention designed to improve social communication, turn-taking, and collaborative skills. Participants work in teams, often acting as "engineers," "suppliers," or "builders" to complete Lego models, which fosters teamwork and problem-solving.
Quiet Lunch
Our Quiet Lunch provision offers a smaller, quieter space where pupils who find the busy dinner hall overwhelming can eat, regulate and practise social skills with familiar adults. It provides discreet pastoral and nutritional support, reduces lunchtime incidents and helps pupils return to afternoon lessons calmer, more focused and ready to learn.

Curriculum
Our curriculum is play-based, exciting and full of opportunities for children to explore, discover, and develop essential skills for life. We believe children learn best when they are engaged, curious, and having fun.
We follow the 7 Areas of Learning within the Early Years Foundation Stage. These are Communication and Language, Personal, Social and Emotional Development, Physical Development, Maths, Literacy, Understanding the World and Expressive Arts and Design. Using the Characteristics of Effective Learning, we encourage children to play and explore, think creatively and keep trying when challenges arise.
Our carefully planned topic cycles spark children's interests and introduce new ideas through hands-on experiences, stories and real-life learning. We adapt our planning to reflect children's interests and next steps, ensuring learning is meaningful and motivating. To make learning even more exciting, we welcome special visitors who enrich our topics and provide memorable experiences. We also celebrate a variety of special events throughout the year, including World Book Day, Science Week and Black History Month.
Children take part in regular PE sessions at school, helping them to develop physical skills, coordination, teamwork and confidence, while becoming familiar with the school environment.
The Pre-School supports early communication and literacy through our pre-phonics programme, with a strong focus on environmental sounds, listening and early phonics, helping children build strong foundations for reading and writing. We also follow White Rose Maths, providing engaging practical maths experiences that help children develop confidence in numbers, counting, shapes, patterns and problem-solving.
Our curriculum includes exciting enrichment opportunities such as our cooking club, where children learn practical life skills, explore new foods, and follow simple instructions. Children also enjoy our Nature Club, where they explore the outdoors , learn about the natural world and develop a love for the environment.
We recognise that children develop at different stages, so we provide different goals and adapt our learning experiences for our two-year-old and pre-school children, ensuring the curriculum is appropriate for all children, and they are supported and challenged appropriately.

Art
Art at Holtspur is taught with a focus on depth, quality, and genuine creative development. We nurture children as artists, encouraging them to think and work like creative practitioners. They develop ideas confidently, refine a range of techniques, and study influential artists linked to each year group’s topics.
Our exceptional outdoor space offers further opportunities for ambitious, expressive work. Throughout their time with us, pupils explore a wide range of art forms—drawing, painting, collage, sculpture, and printmaking—while receiving direct teaching in the essential skills needed for each project. They are encouraged to experiment, analyse the artwork they plan to recreate, and understand its techniques and intentions.
By the end of Year 6, children can discuss a variety of artists, talk confidently about their work, and articulate the skills they have developed.
